title: The Biggest Water Supply Ever Found Isn't on Earth

scenes.text: The biggest body of water ever found holds 140 trillion oceans.
It's not on Earth. It's twelve billion light years away, wrapped around a monster black hole.
That black hole is twenty billion times heavier than our Sun. As it feeds, it pumps out energy that keeps a giant cloud of water vapour warm.
The cloud stretches hundreds of light years. Add it up and it's 140 trillion times all the water in Earth's oceans.
Water forms wherever there's hydrogen, oxygen and a bit of heat, and this quasar supplies all three on a galactic scale.
The twist? That light left the cloud twelve billion years ago. Water was already there, long before Earth existed.

description:
The biggest body of water ever found holds 140 trillion oceans, and it's not on Earth.
In 2011, astronomers using the Caltech Submillimeter Observatory and other telescopes found a cloud of water vapour around the quasar APM 08279+5255, more than 12 billion light years away. Its black hole is about 20 billion times the mass of the Sun, and the vapour spans hundreds of light years.
Where else do you think water is hiding in the universe?
